gappers.catalyst: BitMine Immersion (BMNR) is rallying with the broader ETH complex (ETH +7.95% today) as its Ethereum treasury nears 5.93M ETH (~5% of supply, its 'Alchemy of 5%' goal) and following recent Russell 1000 index inclusion.
gappers.catalyst_detail: BitMine's ETH treasury has grown to 5.74-5.93M tokens plus 206 BTC, with combined crypto/cash/securities near $11.1-15.7B; management says it is close to its internally stated goal of owning ~5% of Ethereum's circulating supply. The company also added recurring revenue via its MAVAN institutional staking platform (~4.88M ETH staked) and was added to the Russell 1000 Index, increasing passive/institutional visibility. Today's move coincides with a broad ETH rally.
gappers.why: BMNR trades largely as a leveraged proxy for ETH: rising Ethereum prices mechanically increase the value of its treasury and staking income, and Russell 1000 inclusion adds forced passive-fund buying on top of that crypto beta.
gappers.impact: The scanner's volume field is stale prior-session volume (72K-1.2M range across the top names), not true premarket volume, so premarket conviction can't be confirmed from this run; the move tracks ETH's own +7.95% day rather than a standalone company event, meaning it is largely crypto-sector beta and would likely reverse if ETH cools. No BMNR-specific negative or one-off headline found.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM - this is ETH-beta plus index-inclusion flow, not a new structural catalyst; durability depends entirely on crypto holding its gains, not on BMNR-specific news.
gappers.opportunity_cost: BMNR is effectively a leveraged single-asset crypto bet, which sits awkwardly inside a stocks-only strategy; its wide 52-week range ($12.80-$65.60) means a stop wide enough to survive normal noise likely can't clear the 2:1 R:R minimum at a sane size. Taking it would use one of the week's 3 new-trade slots and compete directly with BE and OKLO from today's same list for the 20%-per-position cap.

gappers.catalyst: Bloom Energy continues its multi-month re-rating as an AI-data-center power enabler (Brookfield Renewable's up-to-$5B capital-light power partnership, an expanded Oracle fuel-cell deal) with a string of analyst price-target hikes; no distinct same-day headline was found explaining today's specific gap.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Research turned up no fresh, dated news item for today. The standing thesis: Brookfield Renewable agreed to fund up to $5B for a separate entity to buy Bloom's Energy Servers and sell power to data-center customers (removing balance-sheet/financing risk from Bloom), and Bloom expanded its Oracle partnership (up to 2.8GW of fuel cells). Analysts have progressively raised targets (Barclays $254, BTIG $295, Evercore $295, TD Cowen $235) as the stock climbed toward/through the low-$300s over recent months. Today's move looks like continuation of that flow rather than a new discrete event.
gappers.why: Bloom is being repriced from a hardware seller into a capital-light 'power-as-a-service' infrastructure enabler for AI data centers; each incremental partner/analyst datapoint reinforces momentum buying in a name that has already multiplied off its 2025 lows.
gappers.impact: At a reported ~30x sales near all-time highs, this reads as an extended momentum move rather than a fresh anomaly - without a same-day headline, sustainability depends on the broader AI-power theme holding rather than on new BE-specific news; a reversal in AI-capex sentiment would hit this and peer names (peer read-through: the same AI-power-infrastructure trade that has lifted OKLO's long-term thesis, though OKLO itself gapped down today on macro, not this theme).
gappers.horizon: LONG_TERM structurally - the AI power-demand theme aligns with current sector rotation into power/infrastructure - but with no confirmed same-day trigger, any new entry today would be chasing an already-extended move rather than trading a fresh catalyst.
gappers.opportunity_cost: At the 20%-per-position cap, BE would compete with BMNR and OKLO from today's list for the same capital and one of the week's 3 new-trade slots. Absent a fresh dated catalyst, the stop distance needed to survive normal volatility this far into the move likely fails the 2:1 R:R minimum at a sane size - this ranks behind names with a clearer today-dated trigger.

gappers.catalyst: Broad de-risking in speculative, pre-revenue growth/nuclear names as today's August CPI print (8:30 AM ET) firmed and boosted Fed rate-hike bets, per same-day Investing.com coverage; OKLO's standing bull case (federal nuclear-AI initiative with Microsoft/Nvidia, Meta/Switch power-purchase framework deals) is unrelated background, not today's driver.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Investing.com's same-day (Sep 11, 2026) markets coverage reports U.S. consumer prices firmed in August and raised Fed rate-hike bets, with a Fed decision expected the following week. No OKLO-specific negative headline was found; the standing long-term catalyst remains a $200M federal nuclear initiative pairing OKLO with Microsoft and Nvidia (announced Jul 21) plus Meta/Switch power-purchase framework agreements (not yet binding PPAs) and NRC licensing progress.
gappers.why: OKLO is a long-duration, pre-revenue, negative-FCF story stock (Q2 net loss ~$81.6M for H1 2026, ~$3B cash) with no near-term earnings support; a hot CPI print that lifts rate expectations disproportionately discounts far-out cash flows for names like this, and its high short interest (~18.7%) plus weak technicals amplify the move.
gappers.impact: Reads as macro/rate-sensitivity beta rather than an OKLO-specific negative event - no company headline found. Likely read-through to other high-multiple, pre-revenue growth names selling off on the same CPI print today, i.e. a sector/style move rather than an idiosyncratic one.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM for today's CPI-driven dip (rate-driven risk-off tends to fade within days); the structural bull case (federal AI-power nuclear initiative, Meta/Switch framework deals) is LONG_TERM but disconnected from today's move and still needs framework agreements to convert into binding PPAs before it is tradeable on fundamentals.
gappers.opportunity_cost: A -5.62% gap down is not a long entry under this strategy (no catalyst supporting a bounce, no confluence check run this cycle); it only matters here as a name to avoid adding to if already held. It does not compete for the week's 3-new-trade allowance as a long, and a short is outside this strategy's long-bias, stocks-only entry framework.
